== Big Jim Tucker ==

James P. Tucker Jr. (December 31, 1934 – April 26, 2013), commonly known as Big Jim Tucker, was an American journalist and author noted for his extensive coverage of the Bilderberg Group. He became a prominent figure among conspiracy theorists, particularly those concerned with globalization and the influence of powerful elites.

=== Early Life and Career ===
Tucker was born in Fernandina Beach, Florida. He began his career as a sports journalist, working for various newspapers across the United States. His interest in conspiracy theories emerged in the 1970s, focusing primarily on the activities of the Bilderberg Group.

=== Conspiracies and Controversies ===
Jim Tucker is best known for his claims about the Bilderberg Group, an annual private conference of political leaders and experts from industry, finance, academia, and the media. Tucker believed that the group was plotting to create a "New World Order" and exert immense influence over global events. He extensively documented these claims in his book, ''Jim Tucker's Bilderberg Diary,'' where he detailed his attempts to infiltrate their secretive meetings.

Tucker's work was often criticized by mainstream media and subject matter experts for its speculative nature and lack of substantial evidence. Despite this, his reports gained a significant following among those who believed in global conspiracy theories.

=== Connections to Alex Jones ===
Tucker's work dramatically increased in visibility thanks to his association with Alex Jones. Jones frequently hosted Tucker on his show, promoting his findings and contributing to his status within the movement. The two shared the belief that the Bilderberg Group and other elite gatherings had significant and sinister impacts on world affairs.

=== Legacy ===
Tucker remained a controversial figure until his death in 2013. To his followers, he was a dedicated journalist bringing hidden truths to light. Critics, however, viewed him as a purveyor of unfounded conspiracy theories. His work remains influential in conspiracy theory culture, continuing to impact discussions about global power dynamics.

=== Publications ===
* ''Jim Tucker's Bilderberg Diary: One Man's 25-Year Battle to Shine the Light on the World Shadow Government'' (2005)
